 Shri Akshay Jha - Advocate for the objector.
 Order

This first bail application under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is filed on behalf of applicant-Manoj Patel, S/o Rajmani Patel, who is in custody since 21/10/2024 in connection with Crime No.41/2023 registered at Police Station, Hanumana, Distt. Mauganj (M.P)
for offences punishable under Sections 302, 376, 460, 380, 201 of IPC (wrongly mentioned in the order impugned as BNSS).

It is pertinent to mention that the bail application of co-accused, namely, Rakesh Patel (M.Cr.C.
No.48484/2024) was decided by this Court on 25.11.2024.
Shri Pushpraj Singh Gaharwar, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent.
It is submitted that there is no seizure from the present applicant.

Co-accused Rakesh Patel has been enlarged on bail by this court vide order dated 25.11.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.48484 of 2024.
It is further submitted that the applicant is in custody since 21.10.2024 and trial is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:61167 2 MCRC-52862-2024 going to take considerable time for its disposal.
Hence, prayer is made to enlarge the applicant on bail on the ground of parity.

sentences.text: Shri Nitin Kumar Gupta, learned Government Advocate and Shri Akshay Jha, learned counsel for the objector oppose the prayer for grant of bail.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the case diary, as well as keeping in view the principle of parity that similarly placed co- accused, namely, Rakesh Patel has already been enlarged on bail vide order dated 25.11.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.48484/2024, without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court to appear before the said Court on the dates given by the concerned Court during pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
